## Business & Finance

Margins, runway, NPV, VAT, pricing and other business maths. Hub: https://ohfis.com/en/business-finance-tools/

- [Loan Calculator with Amortization Table](https://ohfis.com/en/loan-calculator/): Monthly payment, total interest and a full repayment schedule, with optional extra payments.
  Enter the loan amount, the yearly interest rate and the term. You get the monthly payment, the total interest, the total cost and a month-by-month table of interest, principal and remaining balance. Add an extra monthly payment to see how much interest and time you save.
  How to use: Enter amount, rate and term. Optionally add an extra monthly payment. Read the payment and copy the schedule.
- [Mortgage Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/mortgage-calculator/): Monthly mortgage payment with down payment, tax, insurance and fees, plus the schedule.
  Enter the price, the down payment, the interest rate and the term to see the monthly principal-and-interest payment, the loan-to-value ratio and the total interest over the life of the loan. Add yearly property tax, insurance and monthly fees to see the full monthly cost.
  How to use: Enter price, down payment, rate and years. Add tax, insurance and fees if you want the full cost. Read the payment and the schedule.
- [Simple Interest Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/simple-interest-calculator/): Interest and total for a principal, a yearly rate and a time in years, months or days.
  Simple interest is calculated on the original amount only: interest = principal × rate × time. Enter the principal, the yearly rate and the time as years, months or days (days use a 365-day year).
  How to use: Enter principal and yearly rate. Enter the time and its unit. Read interest and total.
- [Investment Return Calculator (CAGR)](https://ohfis.com/en/investment-return-calculator/): Total return, gain and annualised return (CAGR) between a start and an end value.
  Enter what you invested, what it is worth now and for how many years. You get the gain, the total return in percent and the compound annual growth rate: CAGR = (end ÷ start)^(1 ÷ years) − 1. Add contributions made later to see the gain after all money paid in.
  How to use: Enter start value, end value and years. Optionally add later contributions. Read gain, return and CAGR.
- [Discount Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/discount-calculator/): Sale price, amount saved and the effective discount, also for a second discount on top.
  Enter the original price and the discount percentage to see the price you pay and how much you save. A second discount is applied to the already reduced price, so 20% plus 10% off is 28% in total, not 30%.
  How to use: Enter the original price. Enter the discount (and a second one if you have it). Read the final price and savings.
- [Sales Tax Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/sales-tax-calculator/): Add sales tax to a price or take it out of a total, for any rate.
  Type the price and the tax rate. Choose whether to add the tax to the price or to extract it from a total that already includes tax. State and local rates in the US are added up by you; enter the combined rate.
  How to use: Enter amount and rate. Choose add tax or remove tax. Read net, tax and total.
- [Salary Converter (Hourly, Monthly, Yearly)](https://ohfis.com/en/salary-converter/): Convert pay between hourly, daily, weekly, monthly and yearly with your own working hours.
  Enter one pay figure and say whether it is per hour, day, week, two weeks, month or year. The table shows the equivalent in every other period based on your hours per week, days per week and paid weeks per year.
  How to use: Enter the amount and its period. Set hours, days and weeks. Read every other period.
- [Unit Price Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/unit-price-calculator/): Compare products by price per unit, kilogram or litre and see the best deal.
  Enter the price and size of up to six products, in any consistent unit (g, kg, ml, l, pieces). The calculator works out the price per unit and per 100 and marks the cheapest, showing how much more every other product costs.
  How to use: Enter price and quantity for each product. Read the unit prices. Pick the best deal.
- [Fuel Cost Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/fuel-cost-calculator/): Trip fuel cost and litres from distance, consumption and price, in L/100 km or mpg.
  Enter the distance, your car's consumption and the fuel price. Consumption can be L/100 km, km per litre or miles per US gallon. The result is the fuel needed and the cost, also split between passengers and for a round trip.
  How to use: Enter the distance and choose the units. Enter consumption and price per litre. Read fuel and cost; tick round trip if needed.
- [Margin vs Markup Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/margin-markup-calculator/): Convert between gross margin and markup and find the price from cost.
  Margin and markup both describe profit, but against different bases, and mixing them up is a classic pricing error: a 50% markup gives only a 33% margin. Enter any two of cost, price, margin and markup and see all the others.
  How to use: Choose which two values you know. Enter them. Read the price, profit, margin and markup.
- [Compound Interest Calculator with Chart](https://ohfis.com/en/compound-interest-calculator/): Growth chart for a starting amount, monthly savings, rate and time.
  See how a starting amount and regular deposits grow over time and how much of the final balance is interest. The chart compares your balance with the money you paid in, and the table gives the figures for every year, ready to copy as CSV.
  How to use: Enter the starting amount, monthly contribution, rate and years. Choose how often interest is compounded. Read the final balance and chart, and copy the table.
- [SaaS Runway & Burn Rate Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/saas-runway-calculator/): How many months of cash do you have, with and without revenue growth?
  Enter your cash, monthly costs and current revenue. The calculator shows your net burn, the runway if nothing changes, and the runway if revenue keeps growing at a monthly rate, plus a chart of the cash balance month by month.
  How to use: Enter cash, monthly costs, revenue and growth. Read the runway with and without growth. Adjust costs or growth to see how many months you gain.
- [CAC & LTV Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/cac-ltv-calculator/): Customer lifetime value, LTV:CAC ratio and payback period for subscription businesses.
  Is acquiring customers worth what it costs? Enter average revenue per account, gross margin, monthly churn and CAC to see the lifetime value, the LTV:CAC ratio and the number of months until a customer has paid back their acquisition cost.
  How to use: Enter revenue per account, gross margin, churn and CAC. Read LTV, ratio and payback. Test how lower churn or cheaper acquisition changes the ratio.
- [Break-Even Analysis Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/break-even-calculator/): How many units must you sell to cover fixed costs? With chart and margin of safety.
  Enter fixed costs, the price per unit and the variable cost per unit, and the calculator shows the number of units and the revenue at which you stop losing money, with a chart of revenue against total costs. Add a target profit to see how many more units it takes, and an expected volume to see your margin of safety.
  How to use: Enter fixed costs, price and variable cost per unit. Optionally add a profit target and expected volume. Read the break-even point and the chart.
- [VAT Calculator (Net, Gross & VAT Amount)](https://ohfis.com/en/vat-calculator/): Extract VAT from a gross price or add it to a net price.
  Split a receipt into net amount and VAT, or add VAT to a price. Pick your country to see its current standard and reduced rates, or type any rate, which works equally for GST, sales tax and MwSt.
  How to use: Enter the amount and choose whether it includes VAT. Pick a country or enter the rate. Copy the net, VAT and gross figures.
- [NPV & IRR Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/npv-irr-calculator/): Net present value, internal rate of return and discounted payback of cash flows.
  Evaluate a project by entering the discount rate and a list of cash flows, with the investment as a negative number first. The result is the net present value (NPV), the internal rate of return (IRR), the discounted payback time and a table of discount factors.
  How to use: Enter the discount rate. List the cash flows, one per period, investment first. Read NPV, IRR and payback.
- [Rule of 72 Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/rule-of-72-calculator/): Estimate how many years it takes for money to double at a given rate.
  Divide 72 by the annual rate and you get the approximate number of years it takes for an investment to double: at 8% about 9 years. The calculator shows this estimate next to the exact doubling time, the error and a table for common rates.
  How to use: Enter the annual rate. Read the estimate and the exact value. Use the table to compare other rates.
- [Tiered & Volume Pricing Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/tiered-pricing-calculator/): Model graduated and volume discounts and see the price for any quantity.
  Test a price list before you publish it. Enter tiers as "from quantity, unit price" and a quantity and see the total, the average price per unit, a breakdown by tier and a chart of price against quantity.
  How to use: Enter the tiers, one per line. Choose graduated or volume pricing and a quantity. Check the breakdown and the chart for odd jumps.
- [Sales Commission Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/sales-commission-calculator/): Model tiered commission payouts against a quota.
  Enter the sales achieved, the quota and your commission bands, and see the payout, the quota attainment and a band-by-band breakdown. Typical plans pay a base rate up to quota and accelerators above it.
  How to use: Enter sales and quota. Define the bands as "up to % of quota, rate %". Read the commission and the breakdown.
- [Payment Processing Fee Comparator](https://ohfis.com/en/payment-processing-fee-calculator/): Compare Stripe, PayPal and other fees per payment, per month and per year.
  Find the cheapest way to get paid. Enter a typical payment and how many you receive per month; the table ranks processors by fee, shows what you actually receive, the effective rate and the yearly cost, and the amount you would need to charge to receive exactly 100.
  How to use: Enter a typical payment amount and monthly volume. Edit the processor list to your actual rates. Compare effective rates and yearly cost.
- [Effective Hourly Rate Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/effective-hourly-rate-calculator/): Your real hourly pay after commuting, unpaid overtime and work costs.
  A salary of 60,000 for 40 hours sounds like 28.85 an hour, but the hours that the job really takes are more. Enter commuting time, unpaid extra hours, weeks off and work-related costs to see what you earn for every hour you actually spend.
  How to use: Enter pay, contract hours and weeks off. Add commute, unpaid hours and yearly work costs. Compare the effective and nominal hourly rate.
- [Salary to Contractor Rate Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/salary-to-contractor-rate-calculator/): What hourly or day rate matches an employee salary once benefits, downtime and costs are included?
  Freelancers who simply divide a salary by 2,080 hours undercharge by a third. This calculator adds what an employer pays for you (benefits, pension, insurance), your own business costs, unpaid weeks off and the non-billable time spent on admin and finding clients.
  How to use: Enter the salary you want to match and the benefits percentage. Add your costs, weeks off and billable share. Use the hourly and day rate as the floor for your pricing.
- [ROI Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/roi-calculator/): Return on investment and annualised ROI for campaigns, tools and projects.
  Compare what you put in with what you got back. Enter the cost and the returned value and optionally the time in years, and the calculator shows the ROI percentage, the net gain and the ROI per year, which makes short and long projects comparable.
  How to use: Enter the investment and the value returned. Optionally add the number of years. Read the ROI and the yearly equivalent.
- [Prorated Rent Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/prorated-rent-calculator/): Charge for a partial first month by actual days, a 30-day month or yearly rent.
  When a lease or license starts in the middle of the month, only part of the month is charged. Enter the full monthly amount and the start date to get the first-month charge for the days that remain, including the start day.
  How to use: Enter the full monthly amount and the move-in date. Choose the proration method of your contract. Copy the charge and the daily rate.
- [Group Bill Splitter by Item](https://ohfis.com/en/bill-splitter/): Split a lunch bill by who ordered what, including tax and tip.
  Add the people, list each item with its price and tick who shared it (no one ticked means everyone). Tax and tip are added in proportion to what each person ordered, and you get a clear amount per person to copy into the group chat.
  How to use: Enter the names of the people. Add the items and tick who shared each one. Enter tax and tip and copy the amounts.
- [Depreciation Schedule Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/depreciation-schedule-calculator/): Straight-line, declining-balance and sum-of-years depreciation schedules.
  Enter the cost, the residual value and the useful life, and get a year-by-year schedule with the expense, the accumulated depreciation and the book value, plus a chart. Choose straight line, declining balance (double or another factor) or the sum-of-the-years' digits method.
  How to use: Enter cost, salvage value and useful life. Choose the method. Copy the schedule or download it as CSV.
- [Debt Payoff Planner (Snowball vs Avalanche)](https://ohfis.com/en/debt-payoff-planner/): Compare snowball and avalanche payoff for several loans or cards.
  List your debts with balance, interest rate and minimum payment, enter what you can pay in total each month, and compare the two classic strategies: avalanche (highest interest first) and snowball (smallest balance first). You see the months to debt-free, the total interest and the order in which debts disappear.
  How to use: Enter each debt on its own line. Enter your monthly payment budget. Compare the two strategies and choose one.
- [Customer Churn & Retention Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/churn-calculator/): Project customers and revenue from monthly churn and new sign-ups.
  A monthly churn of 4% sounds small, but it means almost 40% of customers leave within a year. Enter your customers, revenue per customer, monthly churn and new customers per month to see how the base and the monthly revenue develop, and how long it takes to lose half of a cohort.
  How to use: Enter customers, revenue per customer and churn. Add new customers per month and the horizon. Read the projection and the annual churn.
- [Mileage Reimbursement Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/mileage-reimbursement-calculator/): Calculate trip reimbursement with official per-mile or per-kilometre rates.
  Enter the distance and choose a rate (IRS business rate, German travel allowance, UK HMRC, Austrian Kilometergeld, and more) or your own rate to get the reimbursement for a trip, optionally as a round trip.
  How to use: Choose an official rate or enter your own. Enter the distance, and tick round trip if needed. Copy the reimbursement amount.
- [Tip Calculator & Gratuity Table](https://ohfis.com/en/tip-calculator/): Compare tip rates for a business dinner and split the total.
  Enter the bill and the number of people to see the tip, total and amount per person for several rates side by side, so you can choose what is appropriate for the service and the country.
  How to use: Enter the bill and number of people. Edit the list of tip rates if you like. Read the tip, total and share per person.
- [Working Capital & Current Ratio Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/working-capital-calculator/): Compute working capital, current ratio, quick ratio and cash ratio.
  Check whether a business can pay its short-term bills. Enter current assets, current liabilities and the inventory and cash included in the assets to get net working capital and the three standard liquidity ratios.
  How to use: Enter current assets and liabilities. Add the inventory and cash portions. Read the ratios against your industry's norm.
- [Price Elasticity of Demand Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/price-elasticity-calculator/): Estimate how a price change affects quantity and revenue.
  Enter two price points and the units sold at each and learn whether demand is elastic (customers react strongly) or inelastic (they barely react), and what the change did to revenue.
  How to use: Enter the old and new price and the units sold at each. Read the elasticity and its type. Compare revenue before and after.
- [Overhead Cost Allocation Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/overhead-allocation-calculator/): Allocate shared costs to departments by headcount, floor area or revenue.
  Rent, utilities and shared software benefit all teams. Enter the total pool and each department's headcount, floor area and revenue, choose the allocation key and see how many costs each department carries.
  How to use: Enter the cost pool. List departments with headcount, area and revenue. Choose the allocation key and read the shares.
- [Startup Dilution & Cap Table Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/startup-dilution-calculator/): See founders' ownership after seed, Series A and later rounds.
  Enter your funding rounds with the investment and the pre-money valuation and see what the new investors own, how much of the company the founders keep after every round and what that stake is worth at the round's valuation.
  How to use: Enter each round as name, investment and pre-money valuation. Read the ownership after each round and the chart. Vary valuations to see their effect on dilution.
- [Currency Conversion Fee Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/currency-fee-calculator/): See the real cost of an exchange rate margin and transfer fees.
  Enter the amount, the mid-market rate, the provider's margin and any fixed fee, and see how much arrives, the effective rate you really get, and how much money you lose compared with the mid-market rate. Switch to "receive" mode to find out how much you must send so that an exact amount arrives, and add a safety cushion for rate moves when you budget in a foreign currency.
  How to use: Enter the amount and the mid-market rate. Enter the provider margin and fixed fee. Read what arrives, the effective rate and the lost amount.
- [Commercial Lease Cost Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/lease-cost-calculator/): Work out the all-in monthly and total cost of an office or shop lease.
  Landlords quote rent per square foot or square metre per year, but the real cost includes operating costs, taxes and insurance (CAM or triple net charges), fixed extras such as parking, yearly rent escalation and sometimes free months. Enter them and get the cost in year 1 per month, a year-by-year table, the total over the lease term and the true all-in cost per unit of area.
  How to use: Enter the area and the yearly price per unit. Add operating costs, extras, escalation and term. Compare the all-in cost with other offers.
- [Inflation Calculator (Future & Past Value)](https://ohfis.com/en/inflation-value-calculator/): What an amount will cost in the future or is worth today, at an inflation rate you choose.
  Enter an amount, a yearly inflation rate and the number of years to see what the same goods will cost then, how much purchasing power the money loses, or what an amount from the past is worth today. A third mode finds the average annual inflation rate between two prices, for example from a menu from 2010 and today's menu.
  How to use: Choose what to calculate. Enter the amount, rate and years or the two prices. Read the result and the table.
- [Cash Drawer Counter & Float Balancer](https://ohfis.com/en/cash-drawer-counter/): Count notes and coins and compare with the expected amount: over, short or balanced.
  Enter how many of each note and coin are in the till or petty-cash box, and the tool adds them up, compares the total with the amount you expected (opening float plus sales) and shows whether the drawer is over, short or balanced. You can copy the count as a short report for your records.
  How to use: Choose the currency and enter the expected amount. Enter the number of each note and coin. Read the difference and copy the report.
- [Business Model Canvas (Interactive, with Sticky Notes)](https://ohfis.com/en/business-model-canvas/): Fill in the nine blocks of the Business Model Canvas with sticky notes and export it as PNG or Markdown.
  The Business Model Canvas describes a business on one page in nine blocks: customer segments, value propositions, channels, customer relationships, revenue streams, key resources, key activities, key partners and cost structure. Add a sticky note to each block, edit it in place, change its colour and drag notes between the blocks while you discuss the model with your team.
  How to use: Start with the customer segments and the value propositions, then work through the other blocks. Add one idea per sticky note; drag notes to other blocks, recolour or delete them. Download the PNG, copy the Markdown or save the board as a file.
- [Lean Canvas (Interactive, with Sticky Notes)](https://ohfis.com/en/lean-canvas/): Plan a startup on one page: problem, solution, metrics, unfair advantage and more, with sticky notes.
  The Lean Canvas is a one-page plan for new products and startups. Instead of partners and resources it starts from the problem: problem, customer segments, unique value proposition, solution, channels, revenue streams, cost structure, key metrics and unfair advantage. Fill the boxes with sticky notes, move them around, and keep the canvas short enough to test the riskiest assumptions first.
  How to use: Write the top problems and the customer segments first. Add the unique value proposition, solution, channels and the numbers that matter. Export the canvas and test the riskiest assumption with real customers.
- [Eisenhower Matrix with Sticky Notes (Interactive)](https://ohfis.com/en/eisenhower-matrix-board/): Sort tasks as sticky notes into urgent/important quadrants by dragging, then export or print.
  The Eisenhower matrix sorts tasks by two questions: is it urgent, and is it important? Do the urgent and important ones first, schedule the important but not urgent ones, delegate the urgent but unimportant ones and drop the rest. Write each task on a sticky note, drag it to the right quadrant and recolour it by person or project.
  How to use: Add a note in any quadrant and write the task. Drag notes to the quadrant where they belong, or use the menu on the note. Print the matrix or export it as PNG or Markdown.
- [PESTEL Analysis Board (Sticky Notes)](https://ohfis.com/en/pestel-analysis-board/): Map political, economic, social, technological, environmental and legal factors with sticky notes.
  A PESTEL analysis looks at the outside world of a business in six areas: political, economic, social, technological, environmental and legal factors. Add one sticky note per factor, sort them into the six boxes and discuss which ones matter most for your plans.
  How to use: Collect the outside factors that could affect your business. Put each on a sticky note in the matching box. Mark the most important ones by colour and export the board.
- [Porter's Five Forces Board (Sticky Notes)](https://ohfis.com/en/porters-five-forces-board/): Assess an industry with the five competitive forces and collect evidence on sticky notes.
  Porter's Five Forces explain how attractive an industry is: the threat of new entrants, the bargaining power of suppliers and of buyers, the threat of substitutes and the rivalry between existing competitors. Write the facts that support each force on sticky notes and see where the pressure on your margins comes from.
  How to use: Name the industry or market in the board name. Add evidence for each of the five forces on sticky notes. Discuss which forces are strongest and export the board.
- [Empathy Map Canvas (Sticky Notes)](https://ohfis.com/en/empathy-map-canvas/): Understand a customer or user: what they see, hear, say, do, think and feel, with their pains and gains.
  An empathy map puts you in the shoes of one customer or user. Write what this person sees, hears, says and does, what they think and feel, and what hurts them (pains) and what they want (gains). Use real observations from interviews instead of assumptions, and give the board the name of the persona.
  How to use: Name the person or persona in the board name. Fill the boxes with observations from interviews and research. Look for patterns in the pains and gains and export the board.

## Everyday Calculators

Percentages, fractions, averages, age, BMI, calories, pace and a scientific calculator. Hub: https://ohfis.com/en/calculators/

- [Percentage Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/percentage-calculator/): Percent of a number, percentage change, what percent is X of Y, add or subtract a percentage.
  Six everyday percentage questions in one place: what is 15% of 200, what percent is 30 of 200, by how much did a value change from 80 to 100, which number is 15% of what, and what is 100 plus or minus 19%.
  How to use: Choose the question you want answered. Enter the two numbers. Read the result and the formula.
- [Percentage Allocation Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/percentage-allocation-calculator/): Split an amount by percentages or weights, rounded so the parts add up to the cent.
  Divide a total between people, budget lines or categories. Enter the amount and one share per line, either as percentages (50, 30, 20) or as any weights (2, 1, 1); the parts are scaled to 100% automatically.
  How to use: Enter the total amount. List one share per line, optionally with a name. Copy the resulting amounts.
- [Fraction Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/fraction-calculator/): Add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions and mixed numbers, always reduced.
  Type fractions like 3/4, mixed numbers like 1 1/2 or decimals like 0.75 and choose an operation. The result is reduced to lowest terms and shown as a fraction, a mixed number and a decimal.
  How to use: Enter the first and second fraction. Choose +, −, × or ÷. Read the reduced result.
- [Ratio Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/ratio-calculator/): Solve A : B = C : X, and simplify a ratio such as 1920 : 1080 to 16 : 9.
  Use it for recipes, scale drawings, screen sizes and mixing ratios. Fill three of the four fields of A : B = C : D and the fourth is calculated by cross-multiplication. The second part simplifies any ratio to its smallest whole numbers.
  How to use: Fill three of the four fields. Read the missing value. Or enter two numbers to simplify their ratio.
- [Average Calculator (Mean, Median, Mode)](https://ohfis.com/en/average-calculator/): Mean, median, mode, range, sum and count of a list of numbers.
  Paste numbers separated by spaces, commas, semicolons or new lines. You get the arithmetic mean, the median, the mode(s), the minimum, maximum and range, the sum and the count.
  How to use: Paste or type your numbers. Read the statistics. Copy the result.
- [Standard Deviation Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/standard-deviation-calculator/): Sample and population standard deviation and variance of a list of numbers.
  Enter your data and see both the sample standard deviation (divides by n − 1, used when the data is a sample) and the population standard deviation (divides by n, used when you have every value), together with the variances and the mean.
  How to use: Paste your numbers. Read the sample and population values. Copy the figures.
- [Rounding Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/rounding-calculator/): Round to decimals, tens or hundreds, to the nearest 5 or 0.05, with up, down, nearest or banker's rounding.
  Pick how to round (to the nearest value, always up, always down, toward zero, or half to even) and to what precision: a number of decimal places (negative for tens and hundreds) or a step such as 5, 0.5 or 0.05.
  How to use: Enter the numbers, one per line. Choose the method and the precision. Copy the rounded values.
- [Scientific Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/scientific-calculator/): Type an expression with brackets, powers, roots, logarithms, trigonometry and factorials.
  Type a whole expression such as (2+3)*4^2 − sqrt(81) and press Enter. Supported are + − × ÷ % ^, brackets, !, pi and e, sin cos tan and their inverses (degrees or radians), sinh cosh tanh, sqrt cbrt, ln log exp, abs floor ceil round.
  How to use: Type an expression. Choose degrees or radians. Read the result; use a preset to try an example.
- [Random Number Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/random-number-generator/): Draw random integers in a range, with or without repeats, using your browser's secure random source.
  Set a minimum, a maximum and how many numbers you want. Tick "no repeats" to draw without replacement, as for a lottery or a raffle. Numbers come from crypto.getRandomValues, the same secure source browsers use for keys.
  How to use: Enter the minimum, maximum and the count. Choose whether numbers may repeat. Click draw again for a new set.
- [Age Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/age-calculator/): Exact age in years, months and days, days lived and the countdown to the next birthday.
  Enter a date of birth and (optionally) another date to find the exact age, the total number of days, weeks and months lived, and the days until the next birthday. Leave the second date as today to see your age now.
  How to use: Enter the date of birth. Leave "age at" as today or pick another date. Read the result.
- [Pregnancy Due Date Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/pregnancy-due-date-calculator/): Estimate the due date and current week from the first day of the last period.
  Enter the first day of your last menstrual period and the usual cycle length. The estimated due date is 280 days (40 weeks) after the period start, adjusted if your cycle is longer or shorter than 28 days (Naegele's rule).
  How to use: Enter the first day of the last period. Set your average cycle length. Read the due date and current week.
- [BMI Calculator (Body Mass Index)](https://ohfis.com/en/bmi-calculator/): Body mass index, BMI prime and the healthy weight range for your height.
  Enter weight and height in metric or imperial units. BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m)². The result is placed in the WHO categories from underweight to obesity, with BMI Prime (BMI ÷ 25) and the weight range that corresponds to a BMI of 18.5–24.9 for your height.
  How to use: Choose metric or imperial. Enter weight and height. Read BMI, category and healthy range.
- [BMR Calculator (Basal Metabolic Rate)](https://ohfis.com/en/bmr-calculator/): Calories your body burns at rest, with the Mifflin–St Jeor equation.
  Your basal metabolic rate is the energy you use at complete rest. Enter sex, age, weight and height. The Mifflin–St Jeor equation is: 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age + 5 (men) or − 161 (women).
  How to use: Choose sex and units. Enter age, weight and height. Read the BMR in kcal and kJ.
- [Calorie Calculator (Daily Calorie Needs)](https://ohfis.com/en/calorie-calculator/): Daily calories to maintain, lose or gain weight from your activity level.
  Your total daily energy expenditure is the basal metabolic rate multiplied by an activity factor from 1.2 (little exercise) to 1.9 (hard physical work). Eating about 500 kcal less per day loses roughly 0.5 kg a week; 500 more gains about the same.
  How to use: Enter sex, age, weight and height. Choose your activity level. Read the calories for each goal.
- [Body Fat Calculator (US Navy Method)](https://ohfis.com/en/body-fat-calculator/): Estimate body fat percentage from neck, waist and hip measurements.
  Measure your neck and waist (and hips for women) with a tape measure and enter your height. The US Navy formula estimates body fat from the logarithm of these circumferences. The result is shown with the usual category ranges.
  How to use: Choose sex and units. Enter height, neck, waist and (women) hip. Read the percentage and category.
- [Water Intake Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/water-intake-calculator/): Daily water needs from body weight, exercise and hot weather.
  A common rule of thumb is about 33 ml per kg of body weight per day, plus roughly 350 ml for every 30 minutes of exercise and an extra half litre in hot weather. The result is shown in litres, fluid ounces and 250 ml glasses.
  How to use: Enter your weight. Add exercise minutes and hot weather. Read the daily amount.
- [GPA Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/gpa-calculator/): Weighted grade point average from courses, credits and letter grades.
  Add one line per course with its credit hours and letter grade (A to F with plus and minus) or a numeric grade point. The GPA is the sum of credits × grade points divided by the total credits, on the usual 4.0 scale.
  How to use: Add a line per course. Pick the grade and enter the credits. Read the GPA and total credits.
- [Running Pace Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/pace-calculator/): Pace, speed or finish time from distance and time, with race distance presets.
  Enter a distance and the time you ran to get the pace per kilometre or mile and the speed, or enter a target pace to see the finish time. Presets cover 5K, 10K, the half marathon and the marathon, with split times for every unit.
  How to use: Choose km or miles and a distance. Enter your time or a target pace. Read pace, speed and splits.

## IT & Web Tools

Hashes, encoders, cron, JWT, colours, networks and web snippets. Hub: https://ohfis.com/en/it-web-tools/

- [File Checksum Generator (SHA-256, MD5, SHA-1)](https://ohfis.com/en/file-hash-generator/): Calculate and compare file hashes in your browser to verify downloads.
  Download pages publish a checksum so you can check that the file is exactly what the publisher built. Drop the file here, paste the published value and you immediately see whether they match. SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-1 and MD5 can be calculated at once, for files or for typed text.
  How to use: Drop a file (or type text) and choose the algorithms. Optionally paste the checksum from the download page into the compare field. Read the green or red result and copy the hash you need.
- [Subnet Calculator (CIDR, Netmask, IP Range)](https://ohfis.com/en/subnet-calculator/): Network, broadcast, usable hosts and subnet splitting for any IPv4 range.
  Enter 192.168.1.10/24 or an address with a mask such as 10.1.2.3 255.255.0.0 and see the network and broadcast address, the first and last usable host, the number of hosts, the wildcard mask, the binary mask, the address class and whether the range is private, loopback or public. Optionally split the network into equal smaller subnets.
  How to use: Enter an address with a prefix (/24) or a subnet mask. Read the network details. Optionally enter a longer prefix to split the network.
- [Cron Expression Translator](https://ohfis.com/en/cron-expression-translator/): Translate cron schedules into plain English and see the next run times.
  What does "30 4 1,15 * 5" do? Paste a crontab schedule and read it in plain English, then check the next dates it will run. Presets cover common schedules such as every 5 minutes, weekdays at 9:00 or the first of every month.
  How to use: Type or pick a cron expression. Read the plain-English description. Check the list of upcoming runs, in UTC or local time.
- [HTTP Status Codes Reference](https://ohfis.com/en/http-status-codes/): Search every HTTP status code with a plain explanation and a fix.
  Search by number or keyword to see what a status code means and what to do about it. All codes from 1xx to 5xx in the IANA registry that matter in practice are listed, grouped by class, each with a short explanation and a hint for fixing it.
  How to use: Type a code (404) or a keyword (redirect, timeout). Optionally filter by class. Read the explanation and what to try.
- [cURL to JavaScript & Python Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/curl-converter/): Turn a curl command into working fetch and Python requests code.
  API docs and browser dev tools give you curl commands. Paste one and get equivalent JavaScript fetch code and Python requests code with the same method, headers, body, basic auth and form fields.
  How to use: Paste a curl command (in the browser: Network tab → right-click a request → Copy as cURL). Read the generated JavaScript and Python. Copy the code you need.
- [User-Agent String Decoder](https://ohfis.com/en/user-agent-decoder/): Find out browser, OS, device and engine from a user-agent string.
  Paste a user-agent string from a log file or support ticket and see the browser and version, operating system, device type, rendering engine and whether it is a bot. Your own user agent is prefilled.
  How to use: Paste a user-agent string (or use yours). Read the decoded browser, system and device. Treat bot results with care: strings can be faked.
- [HTML Entity Encoder & Decoder](https://ohfis.com/en/html-entity-encoder/): Convert special characters to HTML entities and back.
  Show "<b>" as text on a web page, escape user input or decode &amp;eacute; in scraped text. Choose whether to escape only the five characters that matter in HTML (& < > " ') or also every non-ASCII character, as named entities (&eacute;) or as decimal or hexadecimal numbers (&#233;, &#xE9;).
  How to use: Choose encode or decode. Pick how much to escape. Paste your text and copy the result.
- [Base64 Encoder & Decoder (Text and Files)](https://ohfis.com/en/base64-encoder/): Encode or decode Base64 and data URLs, for text and for files.
  Convert text to Base64 or back, or encode any file by dropping it on the page. The tool detects whether your input looks like Base64 and decodes it automatically, recognises binary results such as images and PDFs and lets you download them, and supports the URL-safe alphabet used in JWTs and web links.
  How to use: Type text, paste Base64, or choose a file. Pick URL-safe, padding and line-length options if needed. Copy the result or download the decoded file.
- [Color Converter (HEX, RGB, HSL, CMYK)](https://ohfis.com/en/color-converter/): Convert colours between HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV and CMYK, with picker and eyedropper.
  Type a colour in any common notation (#2557D6, rgb(37 87 214), hsl(223 70% 48%), cmyk(83 59 0 16) or a name such as coral) and get all the others, ready to copy. Use the picker or, in Chrome and Edge, the eyedropper to sample a colour from anywhere on your screen.
  How to use: Enter a colour or use the picker or eyedropper. Read all formats. Copy the one you need.
- [UUID / GUID Generator (v4 & v7)](https://ohfis.com/en/uuid-generator/): Generate batches of secure random UUIDs, including time-sortable v7.
  Create one UUID or ten thousand: version 4 (random) for general use, or version 7, which starts with a timestamp so IDs sort by creation time and keep database indexes fast. Output formats include upper case, without hyphens, Microsoft braces and SQL-quoted lists.
  How to use: Choose version, quantity and format. Change a setting or press "Generate new batch". Copy the list.
- [Number Base Converter (Binary, Octal, Decimal, Hex)](https://ohfis.com/en/number-base-converter/): Convert integers between bases 2 to 36, with arbitrary size.
  Enter a number in any base from 2 to 36 and see it in binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal and one more base of your choice. Prefixes such as 0x and 0b and underscores are understood, and numbers can be of any size, because the tool uses arbitrary-precision integers instead of floating point.
  How to use: Enter the number and choose its base. Read the other bases. Copy the value you need.
- [Basic Auth Header Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/basic-auth-header-generator/): Create the Authorization: Basic header from a username and password.
  Enter a username and password and get the exact HTTP header, plus the equivalent curl option. Useful for testing APIs, configuring webhooks or setting up a reverse proxy.
  How to use: Enter username and password. Copy the header or the curl option. Use it over HTTPS only.
- [Hex Color Alpha (Opacity to Hex) Calculator](https://ohfis.com/en/hex-alpha-calculator/): Convert opacity percentages to two-digit hex alpha values like 50% = 80.
  Add transparency to a hex colour: enter the opacity in percent, get the two-digit suffix and, with a base colour, the complete 8-digit code (#2557D680). A table lists the usual steps from 0 to 100 percent.

- [Meta Viewport Tag Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/meta-viewport-generator/): Build a correct viewport tag for responsive pages.

  How to use: Choose the width and initial scale. Add viewport-fit if you design for notched phones. Copy the tag into your <head>.
- [Favicon HTML Tag Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/favicon-html-generator/): Generate the link tags and manifest for desktop and mobile icons.

- [URL Query String Builder](https://ohfis.com/en/query-string-builder/): Turn key-value pairs into a correctly percent-encoded URL query string.

  How to use: Enter parameters as key=value lines. Choose how spaces and repeated keys are written. Copy the query string or the full URL.

## Notes & Privacy

Scratchpads, checklists, passwords, QR codes and encrypted notes. Hub: https://ohfis.com/en/notes-tools/

- [Password Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/password-generator/): Create strong random passwords with custom rules, right in your browser.
  Pick the length and character types and get a fresh password with a strength estimate. Options include avoiding look-alike characters (I, l, 1, O, 0) and generating several passwords at once. The password never leaves your device and is not stored.
  How to use: Set the length and the character types. Click "Generate new" until you like the result. Copy it into your password manager.
- [Passphrase Generator (Diceware)](https://ohfis.com/en/passphrase-generator/): Memorable passphrases like correct-horse-battery-staple from the EFF word list.
  A passphrase of five or six random words is much easier to type and remember than a string of symbols, and just as strong. Choose the number of words, a separator and optional capitalisation or a digit, and see the exact entropy.
  How to use: Choose the number of words (six for important accounts). Pick a separator and options. Memorise or store the passphrase; never reuse it.
- [JWT Decoder & Verifier](https://ohfis.com/en/jwt-decoder/): Read a JSON Web Token's header, payload and expiry without sending it anywhere.
  Paste a token and see its header and payload as formatted JSON, with the issued-at, not-before and expiry times converted to dates and a clear "expired" or "valid" status. Enter the secret to check an HS256, HS384 or HS512 signature. Warnings flag unsigned tokens (alg none) and tokens that never expire.
  How to use: Paste the JWT (a leading "Bearer " is fine). Read the header, payload and time claims. Optionally enter the secret to verify an HMAC signature.
- [Wi-Fi QR Code Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/wifi-qr-code-generator/): Make a printable QR code that lets guests join your Wi-Fi with one scan.
  Enter the network name and password, choose the security type and get a QR code that iPhones and Android phones understand: the camera app offers to join the network. Download it as PNG or SVG, or print it for the office, the cafe or the guest room.
  How to use: Enter the network name, security type and password. Download or print the QR code. Test it with a phone before putting it up.
- [vCard QR Code Generator (Contact QR)](https://ohfis.com/en/vcard-qr-code-generator/): Create a QR code that saves your contact details to a phone's address book.

- [QR Code Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/qr-code-generator/): Create QR codes for links, text, email and SMS, free and without tracking.

  How to use: Choose the type of content and enter it. Pick colours and the error correction. Download the PNG or SVG, or print it.
- [Encrypted Note Link (Private Message)](https://ohfis.com/en/encrypted-note-link/): Encrypt a short message in your browser and share it as a link plus a separate key.
  Share a password or a private message without leaving it readable in chat history. Write the note, and you get a link and, separately, a key (or use your own password). Send the two by different channels: whoever has both can read the note.
  How to use: Write your message and choose a random key or a password. Send the link in one channel and the key or password in another. The recipient opens the link, enters the key and reads the note.
- [Online Scratchpad (Auto-Saving Notepad)](https://ohfis.com/en/scratchpad/): A plain notepad that saves automatically in your browser, with several pads.

  How to use: Type in the pad; it saves automatically. Add or rename pads for different topics. Copy or download the text when you need it elsewhere.

  How to use: Add cards in the "To do" column. Drag them to "Doing" and "Done" (or use the arrows). Copy the board as Markdown when you need to report.
