## Team & Meetings

Estimates, decision tools, brackets, pickers and org charts. Hub: https://ohfis.com/en/team-meeting-tools/

- [PERT Estimator (Three-Point Estimate)](https://ohfis.com/en/pert-estimator/): Combine optimistic, likely and pessimistic estimates into expected time and confidence ranges.
  Estimates are uncertain, so ask for three numbers per task: optimistic, most likely and pessimistic. The tool computes the expected duration of each task and of the whole project, the standard deviation, the time within which you can be 80% or 95% sure to finish, and the chance of meeting a target date.
  How to use: List the tasks with optimistic, most likely and pessimistic values. Optionally enter a target total. Read the expected total, the confidence ranges and the probability of hitting the target.
- [Random Name Picker Wheel](https://ohfis.com/en/name-picker-wheel/): Spin a wheel to pick a name for a meeting, a giveaway or a presentation order.
  Paste a list of names and spin: the wheel slows down with a ticking sound and lands on a winner. Remove each winner automatically to pick several people in turn, shuffle the list, and keep a history of winners.
  How to use: Enter the names, one per line. Choose whether winners are removed after a spin. Press "Spin the wheel".
- [Secret Santa Generator](https://ohfis.com/en/secret-santa-generator/): Draw gift partners with exclusions and send each person a private reveal link.
  Enter the participants, add exclusions such as couples who should not draw each other, and generate the draw. Every person gets a private link that reveals only their own match when they tap a button; the organiser can hide the list of pairs to stay surprised too.
  How to use: Enter the participants and any exclusions. Send each person their private link. Participants open the link and tap "Reveal my match".
- [Tournament Bracket Maker](https://ohfis.com/en/tournament-bracket-maker/): Create printable single-elimination brackets or round-robin schedules.
  List the teams or players from best to worst seed and get a bracket for single elimination, with byes where the number is not a power of two, or a round-robin schedule where everyone plays everyone. Download the bracket as PNG or SVG or print it for the hackathon, the office tournament or the school contest.
  How to use: Enter the entrants, best seed first. Choose single elimination or round robin. Download or print the bracket.
- [Org Chart Maker from Indented Text](https://ohfis.com/en/org-chart-maker/): Turn an indented list of people into an organisation chart and download it as an image.
  Type who reports to whom with indentation, optionally as "Name, Title", and get a tidy organisation chart you can download as PNG or SVG for a slide, a wiki page or an onboarding document.
  How to use: Type the structure; indent with spaces or a tab for direct reports. Adjust the box width and colour. Download the chart as PNG or SVG.
- [Passive-Aggressive Tone Checker for Emails](https://ohfis.com/en/tone-auditor/): Highlight guilt-tripping, over-apologising and passive-aggressive phrases with kinder alternatives.
  Before you press send, paste your email or chat message and see which phrases may sound passive-aggressive ("as per my last email"), blaming ("you never"), guilt-tripping, condescending ("obviously"), vague ("ASAP") or over-apologetic. Each flagged phrase comes with a plain suggestion, and messages with too many apologies, exclamation marks or capitals get a gentle note.
  How to use: Paste your draft message. Read the highlighted phrases and the suggestions. Rewrite what could land badly, then send.
- [Brain Dump Organizer (Sort Thoughts into Tasks)](https://ohfis.com/en/brain-dump-organizer/): Paste everything on your mind and get tasks, questions, ideas and worries sorted.
  Write down everything that is on your mind in any order: to-dos, worries, questions, ideas, half sentences. The organiser splits it into items and sorts them into urgent items, tasks, items with a date, questions, ideas, worries and notes, lists the people you mention and gives you a Markdown checklist to copy into your notes or task tool.
  How to use: Type or paste your thoughts, one per line or as sentences. Check the sorted groups. Copy the Markdown checklist.
- [Random Team Generator (Split a Group into Teams)](https://ohfis.com/en/random-team-generator/): Split a list of people into balanced random teams, with optional skill levels and pairs to keep apart.
  Paste the names, choose the number of teams or the people per team, and get a fresh random split with one click. If you add a skill number after a name ("Ann: 4"), the tool deals people in a snake draft so every team gets a similar skill total. Pairs written as "Ann != Ben" are placed in different teams whenever that is possible.
  How to use: Enter one name per line, optionally with a skill number. Choose the number of teams or the team size. Press "Shuffle again" until you like the result, then copy the teams.
- [Planning Poker for Agile Estimation (One Device)](https://ohfis.com/en/planning-poker/): Estimate stories with secret cards on one shared screen, then reveal the votes and see median and spread.
  Planning poker keeps teams from anchoring on the first number they hear: everybody picks a card in secret, then all cards are revealed together. This version needs no server and no accounts. Pass the device around, each player picks a card in turn, and the tool hides the votes until you press "Reveal the cards".
  How to use: Enter the players and the story you want to estimate. Pass the device: each player picks a card in secret. Reveal the cards, discuss differences and start a new round.
- [Retrospective Board (Went Well / To Improve / Actions)](https://ohfis.com/en/retrospective-board/): Collect retro cards in columns, vote with thumbs-up and copy the sorted result as Markdown.
  A retrospective helps a team learn from the last sprint or project. Pick a format, such as "Went well / To improve / Actions", "Start / Stop / Continue", "Keep / Problem / Try" or the Four Ls, add cards to the columns, and vote on the ones that matter most with the thumbs-up button. The cards in every column are sorted by votes.
  How to use: Choose a retrospective format. Type a card in a column and press Enter; vote with the thumbs-up button. Copy the sorted board as Markdown, then clear it for the next retro.
- [RACI Matrix Generator and Checker](https://ohfis.com/en/raci-matrix-generator/): Build a RACI chart for tasks and roles and check that every task has exactly one accountable person.
  A RACI chart says who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed for each task. Type the roles in the first line and one task per line, put R, A, C or I in the cells, and the tool draws the table and checks the two golden rules: every task needs exactly one A, and at least one R.
  How to use: Write the roles in the first line, separated by ; , or a tab. Add one task per line with R, A, C or I under each role. Fix the warnings, then copy the Markdown or download the CSV.
- [Meeting Agenda Planner with Times](https://ohfis.com/en/meeting-agenda-planner/): Turn agenda items with durations into a timed agenda and see when the meeting ends.
  Write each agenda item with its length, for example "Status round; 15", choose the start time, and get a timed agenda with the start and end of every item, the total length and the end of the meeting. Enter how much time you have and the tool warns you when the plan is too long, or shows how many minutes are left.
  How to use: Choose the start time and, optionally, the time you have. List the items as "title; minutes", one per line. Check the end time and copy the agenda into your invitation.
- [SWOT Analysis Maker](https://ohfis.com/en/swot-analysis-maker/): Fill in strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats and get a clean SWOT grid to copy or print.
  A SWOT analysis sorts what matters for a plan into four boxes: internal strengths and weaknesses, external opportunities and threats. Type one point per line in each box and the tool shows the familiar 2 × 2 grid with a title, ready to copy as Markdown or to print.
  How to use: Enter a title for the analysis. Write one point per line in each of the four boxes. Copy the Markdown or print the grid.
- [Priority Matrix Maker (Impact/Effort and Eisenhower)](https://ohfis.com/en/priority-matrix-maker/): Sort tasks into quick wins, big bets, fill-ins and money pits, or into the Eisenhower quadrants.
  Prioritising is easier when you see the options side by side. In the impact/effort view each task gets an impact and an effort from 1 to 5; the tool puts it into quick wins (high impact, low effort), big bets, fill-ins or money pits and sorts every box by the best ratio. In the Eisenhower view you mark each task as urgent and important and get the four quadrants: do now, plan, delegate, drop.
  How to use: Choose impact/effort or the Eisenhower matrix. Enter one task per line with its two values. Read the quadrants and copy them as Markdown.
- [Rotation Schedule Generator (On-Call, Cleaning, Chair Duty)](https://ohfis.com/en/rotation-schedule-generator/): Create a fair rotation of people over days, weeks or fortnights and skip anyone who is away.
  Many teams share a recurring job: being on call, chairing the weekly meeting, taking notes, watering the plants. Enter the people in the order they should take turns, choose the first day and the length of a turn, and the tool lists who is on duty for every period.
  How to use: List the people in the order of their turns. Choose the first day, the length of a turn and how many turns. Add absences, then copy or download the schedule.
- [Team Canvas (Interactive, with Sticky Notes)](https://ohfis.com/en/team-canvas/): Align a team on purpose, goals, values, roles, strengths, risks and working rules, with sticky notes.
  A team canvas helps a new or struggling team agree on the basics on one page: why the team exists (purpose), what it wants to achieve (goals and success criteria), what it stands for (values), who does what (roles and skills), what each person needs, where the team is strong or weak and how it works together (rules and activities).
  How to use: Start with purpose and goals, then values and roles. Let everybody add sticky notes, then sort and discuss them together. Agree on the rules, export the canvas and review it after a few weeks.

## Audio & Video

Tone generators, teleprompter, recorders and display tests. Hub: https://ohfis.com/en/audio-tools/

- [Online Tone Generator (Sine, Square, Sweep)](https://ohfis.com/en/audio-tone-generator/): Play pure tones and frequency sweeps to test speakers and find hums or rattles.
  Play a pure tone at any frequency from 1 Hz to 20 kHz with sine, square, triangle or sawtooth waves, on both speakers or only the left or right one. A 30-second sweep slides from 20 Hz to 20 kHz so you can find the frequency at which a speaker rattles, a cabinet resonates or coil whine appears. The display shows the nearest musical note.
  How to use: Set the volume low, choose a frequency and press Play. Use the channel selector to test left and right, or start the sweep to find a resonance. Stop as soon as you hear the problem frequency and note the value.
- [Online Teleprompter](https://ohfis.com/en/teleprompter/): A full-screen scrolling script with adjustable speed, size and mirror mode.
  Paste your script, set the speed and text size and start: the text scrolls smoothly in full screen while you look into the camera. A red reading line marks where to read, Space pauses, the arrow keys change the speed on the fly, and mirror mode flips the text for teleprompters that read through glass.
  How to use: Paste your script and set the speed and size. Press "Start teleprompter" (full screen). Pause with Space, change speed with ↑ and ↓, close with Esc.
- [BPM Tap Tempo Counter](https://ohfis.com/en/bpm-tap-counter/): Tap along to find the tempo of a song in beats per minute.
  Tap the button or press the space bar on every beat and read the tempo. The tool averages your last twelve taps, shows half-time and double-time values, warns if your taps are uneven and can play a metronome click at the measured tempo.
  How to use: Play the music and tap on every beat (or press Space). Read the BPM after about eight taps. Turn on the click to check it against the song.
- [Audio Normalizer (Make Audio Louder)](https://ohfis.com/en/audio-normalizer/): Bring a quiet recording up to a standard peak or loudness level.
  Drop an audio file (WAV, MP3, M4A, OGG, FLAC or the sound of a video) and raise it to a target level. Peak normalisation makes the loudest point reach the target (−1 dBFS is the usual choice); loudness normalisation matches the average level (about −16 dBFS RMS for podcasts) while keeping the peaks below −1 dBFS. You hear the result before downloading it as WAV.
  How to use: Drop the audio file. Choose peak or loudness mode and the target level. Listen, then download the WAV.
- [Audio Silence Remover & Trimmer](https://ohfis.com/en/silence-trimmer/): Cut silence from the start and end of a recording, or shorten long pauses.
  Drop a recording and let the tool find where the sound really starts and ends. It trims the silent edges, keeps a small padding so that nothing sounds cut off, and can also shorten long pauses inside the recording, for example in a voice memo or a lecture.
  How to use: Drop the audio file. Set the threshold and padding. Listen and download the trimmed WAV.
- [Audio Channel Tool (Mute, Swap, Invert, Pan, Mono)](https://ohfis.com/en/audio-channel-mixer/): Mix to mono, swap or mute left/right, invert polarity or pan a track.
  Fix common problems with stereo files in one step: mix a recording down to mono, swap left and right, silence one channel (for example when a microphone was only recorded on one side), invert the polarity of one or both channels to check phase problems, or place a mono signal anywhere between left and right.
  How to use: Drop the audio file. Choose the operation. Listen and download the WAV.
- [Audio Pitch & Speed Changer](https://ohfis.com/en/audio-pitch-shifter/): Make a recording higher, lower, faster or slower, like a tape.
  Shift a recording by semitones (12 = one octave) or change its speed in percent and download the result as WAV. It is useful to transpose a backing track, slow down a passage to learn it, or fix a recording played at the wrong speed.
  How to use: Drop the audio file. Choose semitones or speed percent. Listen and download the WAV.
- [Online Voice Recorder (with Trim)](https://ohfis.com/en/voice-recorder/): Record from your microphone, check the level, trim and download.
  Press record, speak, press stop. A level meter shows whether the microphone picks you up, a timer shows the length and, when you are done, you can play the recording, cut it to the part you want and download it as WAV, or keep the original browser recording (WebM/OGG/M4A).
  How to use: Allow the microphone and press Record. Press Stop and listen to the result. Set start and end to trim, then download.
- [Online Screen Recorder](https://ohfis.com/en/screen-recorder/): Record a screen, window or tab, with optional audio, and save it as a video file.
  Record a demo, a bug or a tutorial directly in the browser. Choose a whole screen, a window or a browser tab in the browser's own picker, optionally add your microphone and the tab's audio, and download the recording as a video file when you press Stop.
  How to use: Press Start recording and choose what to share. Stop with the button or the browser's sharing bar. Play it back and download the video.
- [Webcam Resolution & Frame Rate Checker](https://ohfis.com/en/webcam-info/): See what resolution and frame rate your camera really delivers.
  Start the camera and read its real resolution, the frame rate it delivers right now (measured live), the maximum resolution and frame rate the camera reports, and its aspect ratio. Request 720p, 1080p, 4K or 60 fps and see what you actually get. Switch between several cameras.
  How to use: Press Start camera and allow access. Choose a camera, resolution and frame rate to request. Read the real values and the measured frame rate.
- [Microphone Noise Floor Test](https://ohfis.com/en/microphone-noise-floor/): Measure the background noise of your room and microphone in dBFS.
  Stay silent for eight seconds and the tool measures the average level of everything your microphone picks up: room noise, fans, electrical hiss. A verdict from "excellent" to "very noisy" tells you if the setup is fine for calls and recordings, and the percentile and peak show whether there were short noises.
  How to use: Allow the microphone and press Measure. Stay quiet for eight seconds. Read the noise floor and the verdict.
- [Online Soundboard (Applause, Buzzer, Drum Roll)](https://ohfis.com/en/soundboard/): Twelve instant sounds for meetings, quizzes and demos, plus your own.
  Big pads for the sounds that liven up a meeting or a quiz: ding, buzzer, drum roll, ta-da, sad trombone, applause, whoosh, airhorn, level up, wrong and correct answer and a timer beep. Press 1–9 and 0 on the keyboard to fire the first ten, change the volume, and add your own audio files as extra pads.
  How to use: Click a pad or press its number key. Set the volume. Optionally add your own sound files.
- [Video Speed Controller (Slow Motion & Fast Forward)](https://ohfis.com/en/video-speed-adjuster/): Preview a video at 0.25× to 4× speed and export the sped-up version.
  Open a video from your device and change its speed with a slider or presets between 0.25× and 4×, with or without keeping the voice pitch natural. The tool shows the new running time and can export the result as a WebM file.
  How to use: Choose a video file. Set the speed and pitch option. Preview, then export if you need a new file.
- [Screen Colour Card (White Balance & Brightness)](https://ohfis.com/en/screen-color-card/): A full-screen grey, white or coloured card for webcam white balance and screen checks.
  Show a neutral grey (18 %), daylight white (6500 K), warm (3200 K) or cool (7500 K) card, any colour you pick, or a grey scale with 256 steps, and go fullscreen. Hold it in front of a webcam to set white balance, use it as a soft light for video calls, or check a display for tint, uneven brightness and stuck pixels.
  How to use: Choose a preset or pick a colour. Press Fullscreen. Hold it in front of the camera or inspect the screen.
- [Browser Hardware Acceleration Check (GPU, WebGL, Video Decode)](https://ohfis.com/en/hardware-acceleration-check/): Find out whether your browser really uses the graphics card.
  If videos stutter, video calls lag or the laptop gets hot, the browser may be rendering in software. This check shows the graphics renderer your browser reports, whether it is a software renderer, whether WebGL, WebGL 2 and WebGPU are available, whether H.264, HEVC, VP9 and AV1 1080p video can be decoded power-efficiently (hardware) and how fast a simple canvas test runs.
  How to use: Open the page; the check runs automatically. Look for ⚠ marks and "software rendering". Enable hardware acceleration in the browser settings and update the graphics driver if needed.
- [Screen Refresh Rate & Frame Drop Test](https://ohfis.com/en/screen-refresh-rate-test/): Measure the real refresh rate, jitter and dropped frames of your browser.
  Is your 144 Hz monitor really running at 144 Hz in the browser? Press measure, watch the moving bar for five seconds and get the measured refresh rate, the nearest standard rate, the average frame time, the jitter (standard deviation of frame times) and the number of slow frames, with advice if the animation is uneven.
  How to use: Close heavy tabs and press "Measure for 5 seconds". Watch the bar for stutter. Compare the Hz with your monitor settings.
- [Aspect Ratio Calculator (16:9, 4:3, Resize)](https://ohfis.com/en/aspect-ratio-calculator/): Find the ratio of a resolution, scale to a new width, and get screen PPI.
  Enter a width and a height and see the exact ratio (1920 × 1080 → 16:9), the closest standard format, the decimal value, the orientation and the megapixels. Add the screen diagonal for the pixel density and physical size, or a target width to get the matching height.
  How to use: Enter width and height. Optionally add a diagonal or a target width. Read the ratio, closest standard and sizes.
- [Dual Monitor Size & Scaling Matcher](https://ohfis.com/en/dual-monitor-matcher/): Compare two screens and find the scaling that makes text the same size.
  Enter resolution and diagonal of both monitors. The calculator shows the pixel density of each, the physical size, the height difference and the display scaling to set so that windows and text look equally large on both screens when you drag them across.
  How to use: Enter the resolution and diagonal of both monitors. Read the density ratio and the advice. Set the scaling in the operating-system display settings.
- [Video Frame Capture (Screenshot from Video)](https://ohfis.com/en/video-frame-capture/): Pick the exact frame in a video and save it as a full-resolution PNG or JPEG.
  Open a video from your device, scrub to the moment you want, step frame by frame or second by second and save the frame as a PNG or JPEG at the full resolution of the video. Saved frames are listed with their time code so you can collect several.
  How to use: Choose the video. Scrub or step to the frame. Press "Save frame".
- [Audio Cutter (Trim MP3 and WAV Online)](https://ohfis.com/en/audio-cutter/): Cut a part out of a recording or keep only the part you need.
  Drop an audio file, enter where the part you want starts and ends, and save it as WAV or MP3. You can keep only that part (to make a ringtone, a sound bite or a trimmed interview) or cut it out and join the rest (to remove a cough or a mistake). Optional fade in and fade out avoid clicks at the cut points.
  How to use: Drop the audio file. Choose "keep" or "remove", then enter start and end in seconds. Listen to the preview and download the WAV or MP3.
- [Audio Joiner (Merge MP3 Files Online)](https://ohfis.com/en/audio-joiner/): Join several audio files into one, in the order you choose.
  Add two or more audio files, put them in the right order with the arrow buttons and download one combined file as WAV or MP3. A crossfade of a few hundred milliseconds lets one track flow into the next, for example for a mix or a podcast with intro and outro music.
  How to use: Add the audio files. Order them with ↑ and ↓ and remove any you do not need. Set a crossfade if you like, listen, and download the result.
- [Change Audio Volume (Make MP3 Louder or Quieter)](https://ohfis.com/en/audio-volume-changer/): Make a recording louder or quieter by a number of decibels.
  Enter how many decibels louder (+) or quieter (−) the recording should be, listen to the result and save it as WAV or MP3. +6 dB is roughly twice as loud, −6 dB half. Fade in and out can be added in the same step.
  How to use: Drop the audio file. Enter the change in dB (positive = louder). Check the preview and the clipping note, then download.
- [Reverse Audio (Play Sound Backwards)](https://ohfis.com/en/audio-reverser/): Turn a recording around so that it plays backwards.
  Drop a recording and get it back reversed, ready to play or download as WAV or MP3. Reversed sound is used for effects in music and video, for puzzles and for fun with spoken words.
  How to use: Drop the audio file. Listen to the reversed version. Download it as WAV or MP3.
- [Audio Equalizer (Bass and Treble Online)](https://ohfis.com/en/audio-equalizer/): Shape the sound of a recording with five frequency bands and presets.
  Pick a preset (bass boost, treble boost, voice clarity, warm and soft) or set five bands yourself: 60 Hz, 250 Hz, 1 kHz, 4 kHz and 12 kHz, each from −12 to +12 dB. The result is rendered, played back for you to check and saved as WAV or MP3.
  How to use: Drop the audio file. Choose a preset or move the five bands. Listen and download.
- [Audio Converter (to MP3 or WAV)](https://ohfis.com/en/audio-converter/): Convert M4A, OGG, FLAC, Opus or video sound to MP3 or WAV.
  Drop an audio file and save it as MP3 (small, plays everywhere) or WAV (uncompressed, for editing). It also pulls the sound track out of a video file such as MP4 or WebM. Choose the MP3 bitrate from 64 to 320 kbps and, if you like, convert to mono to halve the size.
  How to use: Drop the audio or video file. Choose MP3 or WAV and the quality. Download the converted file.
- [Webcam Video Recorder](https://ohfis.com/en/webcam-video-recorder/): Record a video from your webcam and save it, without installing anything.
  Turn the camera on, pick the camera and the resolution, press record and save the video as a file. It is made for a quick message, a video application, a screen-less demo or a test of your camera and microphone. The preview is mirrored like a mirror, the saved video is not.
  How to use: Press "Turn camera on" and allow access. Choose camera, resolution and whether to record sound. Press "Start recording", then stop and download the video.
- [Text to Speech (Read Text Aloud)](https://ohfis.com/en/text-to-speech/): Have your browser read a text aloud with a voice and speed you choose.
  Paste a text, choose one of the voices on your device, set speed, pitch and volume and press play. Useful for proofreading (mistakes are easy to hear), for learning pronunciation or for listening to an article instead of reading it. Pause, resume and stop at any time.
  How to use: Type or paste the text. Choose the voice (it should match the language of the text) and the speed. Press "Read aloud".
- [Audio Noise Reducer (Remove Background Noise)](https://ohfis.com/en/noise-reducer/): Reduce steady hiss, hum and fan noise in a recording.
  Drop a recording and reduce steady background noise such as hiss, hum, fan or traffic rumble, by 6 to 40 dB. The noise level is learned automatically from the quietest tenth of the recording, or from a stretch you mark as noise-only, and then pushed down wherever the sound is not clearly louder than the noise. Listen to the result, compare, and download WAV or MP3.
  How to use: Drop the recording. Set the reduction and, if you know a noise-only stretch, its start and end. Listen to the preview and download the result.
- [BPM and Key Detector (Find Tempo and Key of a Song)](https://ohfis.com/en/bpm-key-detector/): Find the tempo in BPM and the musical key of an audio file.
  Drop a song or a recording and get its tempo in beats per minute, the half and double tempo, other candidates, the musical key (such as A minor) and the Camelot code used by DJs for harmonic mixing. Useful to match tracks, to practise along or to label a sample library.
  How to use: Drop the audio file. Wait a moment while it is analysed (up to 3 minutes from the middle of the song). Read the tempo, key and the alternatives.

## Video Tools

Trim, join, convert, compress, crop, resize and edit videos without uploading them. Hub: https://ohfis.com/en/video-tools/

- [Video Trimmer (Cut Video Online)](https://ohfis.com/en/video-trimmer/): Cut a video to the part you need, with or without re-encoding.
  Drop a video, play it, pause where the part you want starts and ends, press "use current position" and save the trimmed video. Fast mode copies the streams without re-encoding, so even a long video is cut in seconds without any loss of quality; the cut then snaps to the nearest keyframe. Normal mode re-encodes and is accurate to the frame.
  How to use: Drop the video and play it. Set start and end (or use the current position of the player). Choose fast or accurate mode and press "Trim video".
- [Video Merger (Join Videos Online)](https://ohfis.com/en/video-merger/): Join several clips into one video, in the order you choose.
  Add two or more clips, order them with the arrow buttons and get one video. Clips with a different size or frame rate are fitted into one frame (the first clip’s size, or a size you pick) with black bars, so a phone clip and a screen recording can be combined without distortion.
  How to use: Add the video clips. Order them and choose the frame size. Press "Join videos" and download the result.
- [Video Converter (MP4, WebM, GIF, MP3)](https://ohfis.com/en/video-converter/): Convert videos between MP4, WebM and GIF, or take just the sound as MP3.
  Drop a video and convert it to MP4 (H.264, plays on every phone, TV and browser), WebM (VP8, for websites), an animated GIF or an audio file (MP3, M4A, WAV). You can limit the width, remove the sound and choose between fast and high-quality encoding.
  How to use: Drop the video. Choose the target format and, if you like, a maximum width. Press "Convert" and download the file.
- [Video Compressor (Reduce Video File Size)](https://ohfis.com/en/video-compressor/): Make a video file much smaller for email, chat or upload.
  Drop a video, choose how strongly to compress it and, if the picture does not need to be big, a smaller height such as 720p, and get a much smaller MP4. A phone video of 500 MB often shrinks to a fifth with no visible loss for sharing.
  How to use: Drop the video. Choose the quality (CRF) and, if you like, a maximum height. Press "Compress video" and compare the sizes.
- [Crop, Rotate and Flip Video](https://ohfis.com/en/video-crop-rotate-flip/): Crop to an aspect ratio or area, rotate by 90° steps and mirror a video.
  Fix a sideways phone video, cut a landscape clip to a vertical 9:16 format for Stories and Reels, make a square 1:1 version or mirror a selfie video. Crop to a standard aspect ratio around the centre or draw an exact rectangle (the red frame on the preview shows what stays), then rotate in 90° steps and flip horizontally or vertically.
  How to use: Drop the video. Choose the crop (ratio or rectangle), rotation and flips. Press "Apply" and download.
- [Video Resizer (Change Video Resolution)](https://ohfis.com/en/video-resizer/): Scale a video to 1080p, 720p, 480p or an exact size.
  Choose a standard height such as 1080p, 720p or 480p, a width, or an exact width and height, and get a scaled MP4. Smaller videos are faster to upload, take less space and play smoothly on weak connections.
  How to use: Drop the video. Choose the height, width or exact size. Press "Resize video" and download.
- [Change Video Speed (Slow Motion and Fast Forward)](https://ohfis.com/en/video-speed-changer/): Slow a video down or speed it up, with the sound following.
  Enter a speed from 0.1× to 20×: 0.5 plays at half speed (slow motion), 2 at double speed, 8 makes a timelapse out of a long recording. The sound is adjusted to the same speed without changing its pitch.
  How to use: Drop the video. Enter the speed (below 1 = slower, above 1 = faster). Press "Change speed" and download.
- [Loop Video (Repeat a Video)](https://ohfis.com/en/video-loop/): Repeat a clip several times to make a longer video.
  Enter how many times the clip should play in total (2 to 200) and get one longer video: for a background loop on a screen, a meditation or ambient clip or a short animation that should run for minutes.
  How to use: Drop the video. Enter how often it should play. Press "Make loop" and download.
- [Change Video Volume or Mute a Video](https://ohfis.com/en/video-volume-changer/): Make the sound of a video louder or quieter, or remove it.
  Raise or lower the volume of a video by a number of decibels, or remove the sound completely. +6 dB is about twice as loud, −6 dB half. Useful for a recording that is too quiet, a video with loud music or one that should be silent before you add your own music.
  How to use: Drop the video. Enter the volume change in dB, or tick "remove the sound". Press "Apply" and download.
- [Add Audio or Music to a Video](https://ohfis.com/en/video-add-audio/): Replace the sound of a video with music or a voice-over, or mix both.
  Choose a video and an audio file (MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG, FLAC) and either replace the original sound or mix both, with separate volume controls. Good for putting music under a silent clip or a voice-over onto a screen recording.
  How to use: Drop the video and choose the audio file. Choose replace or mix and set the volumes. Press "Add audio" and download.
- [Add Text to a Video](https://ohfis.com/en/video-add-text/): Put a title, caption or message on a video, at a position and time you choose.
  Type a text, choose size, colour and one of nine positions, optionally a dark box behind it for legibility and a start and end time, and get the video with the text burned in. Good for titles, captions, a name, a date or a call to action.
  How to use: Drop the video. Type the text and choose size, colour and position. Set the time range if needed, press "Add text" and download.
- [Add Image or Logo to a Video](https://ohfis.com/en/video-add-image/): Place a logo or picture on a video, with size, opacity and timing.
  Choose a video and a picture (a PNG with a transparent background works best for logos), pick one of nine positions, the size as a share of the video width, the opacity and, if you like, when it should appear. Use it to watermark your own videos or to add a channel logo.
  How to use: Drop the video and choose the image. Set position, size, opacity and timing. Press "Add image" and download.
- [Remove Logo or Watermark from a Video](https://ohfis.com/en/video-logo-remover/): Smooth over a small logo or mark in a corner of a video.
  Enter the position and size of the logo (the red frame on the preview shows the area) and the area is filled in from its surroundings. It works well for small, static logos on calm backgrounds, such as a corner mark on your own footage or a timestamp.
  How to use: Drop the video. Enter left, top, width and height of the logo area and check the red frame. Press "Remove logo" and download.
- [Video to GIF Converter](https://ohfis.com/en/video-to-gif/): Turn a part of a video into an animated GIF with good colours.
  Choose where the GIF starts, how long it runs, the frames per second and the width, and get an animated GIF. A few seconds at 10–15 frames per second and 480 px wide makes a handy reaction or demo GIF.
  How to use: Drop the video and set the start with "use current position". Choose length, frame rate and width. Press "Make GIF" and download.
- [Video Stabilizer (Reduce Camera Shake)](https://ohfis.com/en/video-stabilizer/): Smooth out small shakes in hand-held video.
  Drop a shaky hand-held clip and get a calmer version. Set how large a shake may be corrected (search range in pixels) and whether the edges that appear when the picture is shifted are filled by mirroring or left black.
  How to use: Drop the video. Choose the search range and the edge handling. Press "Stabilise", compare with the original and download.
